notes: Rn-222 epsilon = EMANATION coefficient, kept as a documented UPPER BOUND of the effective exhalation fraction (D60): moisture raises emanation up to 5x (S0242) or 15-40x (S0243) while saturated pores cut the release that reaches air, so a ponded deposit exhales far less. Low 0.005 traced: Kovler dry 0.0052 (S0244), Sakoda A5 VA85 0.005-0.007 (S0242), Barton dry pulverised ash about 0.003-0.009 (S0243 Fig. 3). Central 0.03 = Sakoda mean for fly ash, n=46 (S0242 Table 3; a maximum-over-moisture mean). High 0.13 -> 0.15: Barton peak at 20 wt% moisture (S0243 Fig. 3); Sakoda range top 0.35 is one sample, not adopted; Solecki 0.08-0.13 (S0247) and TRS 474 <0.1 (S0203) also inside. Rn-220 epsilon = EFFECTIVE EXHALATION (D60), converted from the emanation proposal 0.002/0.01/0.1 (research/coal/papers_round2_radon_content.md Q1; analogy 0.3-0.7 x Rn-222, no Rn-220 measurement exists) with the slab factor f = (L/H) tanh(H/L), L = Rn-220 diffusion length 0.005/0.01/0.02 m, H = deposit thickness 4-15 m (central geometric mean 7.75 m). low = 0.002 x f(0.005, 15) = 0.002 x 0.000333 = 6.7e-07; central = 0.01 x f(0.01, 7.75) = 0.01 x 0.00129 = 1.3e-05; high = 0.1 x f(0.02, 4) = 0.1 x 0.005 = 0.0005; capped at the emanation values. Full arithmetic in research/coal/factors_notes.md. H 4-15 m from research/seepage/notes.md (ponded and landfilled ash). Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): Generic Kd-retardation flush M1 (I 7-100 mm/a, H 4-15 m, rho_b 1000-1600 kg/m3, theta 0.35, Kd Ra 71-2500 L/kg), log-uniform Monte Carlo P5/P50/P95 = 6.9e-7 / 6.4e-6 / 5.9e-5. No direct ash-pond radionuclide measurement found. Almahayni (S0950) Kd are 10% of the geometric mean (conservative); implied Ra s from its leachate maxima 2.6e-7 to 2.4e-4 per a (thin 0.3 m layer). U would be about 30x higher, Pb-210 about 5x lower (notes section 4). Alkaline ash (pH above 8) lowers U Kd (S0955) and raises U share.

Rn-222 epsilon = EMANATION coefficient, kept as a documented UPPER BOUND of effective exhalation (D60). Previously 0.5/0.75/1.0 x fly ash (Phase 1, no data); now coarse stoker ash from Barton Table 2 (S0243): 9.6e-4 dry, 0.016-0.020 at 10-20 wt%, maximum 0.041; Sakoda A5 coarse fractions 0.005-0.045 (S0242). Analogue only (PSPP is a mixed stoker ash). 0.001/0.02/0.05 (was 0.0025/0.0225/0.13). Rn-220 epsilon = EFFECTIVE EXHALATION (D60), converted from the emanation proposal 0.001/0.01/0.04 (research/coal/papers_round2_radon_content.md Q1; analogy 0.3-0.7 x Rn-222, no Rn-220 measurement exists) with the slab factor f = (L/H) tanh(H/L), L = Rn-220 diffusion length 0.005/0.01/0.02 m, H = deposit thickness 4-15 m (central geometric mean 7.75 m). low = 0.001 x f(0.005, 15) = 0.001 x 0.000333 = 3.3e-07; central = 0.01 x f(0.01, 7.75) = 0.01 x 0.00129 = 1.3e-05; high = 0.04 x f(0.02, 4) = 0.04 x 0.005 = 0.0002; capped at the emanation values. Full arithmetic in research/coal/factors_notes.md. H 4-15 m from research/seepage/notes.md (same ponds and landfills as fly ash). Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade D): Same triple as fly ash. Coarser and less reactive, but sluiced to ponds (wetter), so no basis to move the central value either way. No bottom-ash-specific leaching data found.

Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): M4: s = I C_sat /(H rho_b), C_sat 2.5-3.1 kg/m3 gypsum (S0964), rho_b 900-1200 kg/m3, gives P5/P50/P95 2.3e-6 / 9.3e-6 / 3.8e-5 assuming Ra releases congruently with Ca (upper limit; Ra re-uptake by barite lowers it). Low set to the M1 sorption-limited P5. Covers wet-stack and landfilled gypsum only; gypsum in wallboard is Dispersed. Dry-scrubber (CaSO3) and FBC residues not covered.

description: Radium-bearing sludge from coal mine water treatment
notes: Rn-222 epsilon = EMANATION coefficient, kept as a documented UPPER BOUND of effective exhalation (D60); first values (was empty; default 0.2). Type A (Ba-Ra sulphate) sludge: barite scale 0.020-0.063 (S0991, INEL, abstract only), Sakoda mineral 0.03 (S0242); type B (Ra adsorbed on sediment, soil-like): Sakoda soil 0.20; central about the geometric blend of 0.04 and 0.2. Michalik's flux-based effective fractions 0.002-0.07 (S0251) are consistent with the effective value lying below this emanation bound (low confidence). Rn-220 epsilon = EFFECTIVE EXHALATION (D60), converted from the emanation proposal 0.01/0.05/0.2 (research/coal/papers_round2_radon_content.md Q1; analogy 0.3-0.7 x Rn-222, no Rn-220 measurement exists) with the slab factor f = (L/H) tanh(H/L), L = Rn-220 diffusion length 0.005/0.01/0.02 m, H = deposit thickness 0.5-3 m (central geometric mean 1.22 m). low = 0.01 x f(0.005, 3) = 0.01 x 0.00167 = 1.7e-05; central = 0.05 x f(0.01, 1.22) = 0.05 x 0.00816 = 0.00041; high = 0.2 x f(0.02, 0.5) = 0.2 x 0.04 = 0.008; capped at the emanation values. Full arithmetic in research/coal/factors_notes.md. H 0.5-3 m is my assumption for settled sludge and pond sediment (no sludge thickness in the md or the seepage notes; S0251 says wet sediments emit only from the top 0.1-0.2 m); not sourced. Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): S0225 batch tests at L/S 10 with 10 g/L NaCl: Ba-carrier deposits (type A) release 0.004% of Ra; adsorbed-Ra sediments without Ba (type B) 5-7%; type A about three orders lower than B. Triple spans A (low, M2 P5) to B (high, M2 P95 7e-5); central = geometric mean of the A and B medians (1.1e-8, 1.6e-5), because the sludge mix is unknown. BaCl2-treated sludge is type A; settling-pond sediment is type B.
